=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3927-3940 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Issue #4813 adds body to the gh issue list --json field lists, which increases the size of merged_json and ready_json. These lists are then passed to jq as --argjson command-line arguments. Linux caps a single argument string at 131072 bytes (MAX_ARG_STRLEN). Two or three issues with large bodies can exceed this limit, causing jq to fail with "Argument list too long". The || echo "[]" fallback silently produces an empty queue, and the sweep closes nothing with no log line indicating the failure.
  WHY: A malicious or accidental issue body of 65536 characters (GitHub's limit) with an ai:merged label will push the merged_json argument past 131072 bytes when combined with other issues. jq fails to start, the fallback returns [], and the sweep silently skips every issue. The plan for issue #4955 acknowledges this and provides a fix (stdin-fed jq), but that fix has not been implemented in this PR.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:226-229 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The awk -F '\t' field separator relies on GNU awk's extension where \t in ERE matches a literal tab. On non-GNU awk implementations (BSDs, busybox), \t would match a literal backslash followed by t, not a tab character. The function would fail to find issue numbers in ISSUE_INTEGRATION_BRANCHES, returning empty for integration branches, which would block labeling for legitimate integration-branch merges (fail-closed).
  WHY: If the runner image ever switched to a non-GNU awk or if the script ran in a different environment, integration-branch merges would be treated as non-target-branch merges, and issues would not receive ai:merged labels. In the CI runner environment (Ubuntu with gawk) this does not reproduce today.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3931-3942 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: This PR adds `body` to both `gh issue list --json` field lists (lines 3917, 3924), so `merged_json`/`ready_json` now carry every labelled issue's full body. Those payloads are then passed to `jq` as `--argjson` command-line arguments. Linux caps a single argv string at MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 131,072 bytes; GitHub allows 65,536-char issue bodies, so two or three large bodies on `ai:merged`/`ai:ready-to-merge` issues exceed the cap. When that happens `jq` fails to start (`Argument list too long`) and the `|| echo "[]"` fallback silently turns the work queue into an empty list, so `close_merged_issues_sweep` closes nothing for the whole cycle with no log line saying why.
  WHY: Any user who can open/edit an issue that later carries `ai:merged` or `ai:ready-to-merge` can disable the close sweep for every issue by posting large bodies — a denial-of-service of the automated issue-closure path. This is a regression introduced by this PR: before #4813 the payloads held only `number,labels` and stayed far below the limit. The included `docs/plans/issue-4955-close-sweep-large-issue-bodies-plan.md` documents this exact finding (STRIDE: Denial of Service, confidence 10/10) and its Rollout states the fix is intended to "reach main with #4813's final PR (#4826)" — i.e. land in this PR — but the fix code (stream the payloads to `jq` via stdin and surface `queue_build_failed`) is not present here.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
